author: श्रीमदानन्दतीर्थभगवत्पादाचार्य
commentary: तदुपायमाह - कर्मजमिति ॥ कर्मजं फलं त्यक्त्वा, अकामनया ईश्वराय समर्प्य, बुद्धियुक्ताः सम्यग्ज्ञानिनो भूत्वा पदं गच्छन्ति । सयोगकर्म ज्ञानसाधनम् ; तन्मोक्षसाधनमिति भावः ॥ ५१ ॥
translation: Krishna states the practical method (Upāya) to achieve that supreme liberation by using the words beginning with “Karma-jam” (born of action). Renouncing the material fruits and rewards that are born out of performing actions by completely offering those actions to the Supreme Lord (Īśvara) without any selfish desire (Akāmanayā) and thereby becoming endowed with steady spiritual intelligence (Buddhi-yuktāḥ), turning into fully enlightened knowers of reality (Samyag-jñāninaḥ) they confidently go to and attain the supreme, eternal abode (Padam) The underlying intent (Bhāvaḥ) is that action performed in the spirit of Yoga (selfless duty offered to God) is the direct instrument to gain spiritual knowledge (Jñāna-sādhanam) and that spiritual knowledge, in turn, is the ultimate instrument to achieve final liberation (Mokṣa-sādhanam).
